subject: Biology
title: Primary & Secondary Productivity: GPP vs NPP
topic: Gross Primary Productivity, Autotrophic Respiration Losses R, Net Primary Productivity, & Secondary Productivity
quickSummary: Ecosystem productivity: Rate of organic biomass synthesis per unit area over time (g/m²/yr or kcal/m²/yr). Primary Productivity: Rate of organic matter synthesis by autotrophic producers. Gross Primary Productivity (GPP): Total rate of organic matter production during photosynthesis. Net Primary Productivity (NPP): Biomass remaining after autotrophic respiratory losses (R): NPP = GPP - R. NPP is the actual organic biomass available to heterotrophic consumers. Secondary Productivity: Rate of new organic matter synthesis by consumers.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) represents total photosynthetic carbon fixation. Subtracting autotrophic respiratory losses (R) yields Net Primary Productivity (NPP = GPP - R), which fuels all heterotrophs in the ecosystem.

GROSS vs NET PRIMARY PRODUCTIVITY
                    
   GROSS PRIMARY PRODUCTIVITY (GPP) ──► Total rate of organic matter synthesis during photosynthesis.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 Productivity Metrics & Units
- **Productivity** is defined as the rate of biomass or organic matter production per unit area over a specified time interval.
- Expressed as:
  - **Biomass units**: $\text{g/m}^2/\text{year}$ or $\text{dry weight (tonnes/ha/yr)}$.
  - **Energy units**: $\text{kcal/m}^2/\text{year}$ or $\text{J/m}^2/\text{year}$.

### 2.2 Primary Productivity (GPP vs. NPP)
1. **Gross Primary Productivity (GPP)**:
   - The total rate of conversion of solar radiant energy into chemical bond energy (organic matter) by autotrophic green plants during photosynthesis per unit area per unit time.
2. **Autotrophic Respiration Losses ($R$)**:
   - A considerable fraction of gross photosynthate is continuously consumed by the plants themselves to fuel cellular metabolic processes, maintenance, and growth.
3. **Net Primary Productivity (NPP)**:
   - The net organic biomass accumulated and stored in plant tissues that remains after subtracting respiratory costs:
     $$\mathbf{\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R}$$
   - **HIGH-YIELD EXAM INVARIANT**: **NPP represents the actual, usable biomass available for consumption by heterotrophic organisms** (herbivores, carnivores, and decomposers).

### 2.3 Secondary Productivity
- **Secondary Productivity**: The rate of formation of **new organic biomass by heterotrophic consumers** (herbivores and carnivores) per unit area per unit time.
- Driven entirely by assimilating and transforming consumed plant or animal tissues into animal body mass.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Net Ecosystem Productivity (NEP)
conceptBreakdown.title: Net Ecosystem Productivity (NEP)
conceptBreakdown.content: Net Ecosystem Productivity accounts for total ecosystem respiration (autotrophic R_A + heterotrophic R_H): NEP = GPP - (R_A + R_H); positive NEP indicates the ecosystem acts as a net carbon sink accumulating organic carbon.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Light and Dark Bottle Oxygen Method
conceptBreakdown.title: Light and Dark Bottle Oxygen Method
conceptBreakdown.content: Gaarder and Gran's classic method measures aquatic productivity: Dissolved oxygen change in light bottle = GPP - R = NPP; Oxygen decrease in dark bottle = R; GPP is calculated by adding R to NPP.
